scope: Bounded official-source search for enacted 2014-2015 administrative instruments and identity continuity of Bugarama, Muhuta, Muha, and Ntahangwa; no geometry, observer, physical, or native-diagnostic work performed.

sources_opened.title: Loi n°1/10 du 26 mars 2015 portant création de la Province de Rumonge et délimitation des Provinces de Bujumbura, Bururi et Rumonge
sources_opened.source_character: Promulgated text headed République du Burundi / Cabinet du Président, read through FAOLEX-hosted PDF extraction (3 pages). The PDF's OCR heading is noisy, but its title, articles, and closing date consistently identify law 1/10 of 26 March 2015.
sources_opened.read_status: Opened and read extracted text across all three pages, especially page index 1, Articles 1–5. One subsequent normal network GET succeeded; the retained file is inventory/bdi-law-1-10-2015.pdf, 88,657 bytes, SHA256 07197f33c7d380a8cd4274659c3e3bf06f6e582f196ee215db73b89ea018cb6f.
specific_text: Article 2 lists Commune de Bugarama and Commune de Muhuta among five communes constituting Rumonge Province.
Article 2 says: Ces communes gardent leurs délimitations actuelles.
Articles 4 and 6 similarly state that communes in Bujumbura and Bururi keep their current delimitations.
Article 9 says the law enters into force on promulgation; closing line gives 26 March 2015.
sources_opened.implication_limit: This enacted instrument removes the specific claim that the March 2015 provincial transfer itself redrew Bugarama or Muhuta commune limits: it expressly preserves their then-current limits. It does not establish the capture date of the 2007-labeled geospatial features, prove that the retained geometry depicts those limits, or establish any 2023/current sub-commune membership. Thus it materially strengthens historical identity continuity for Bugarama/Muhuta, but does not alone qualify their retained geometries or clear all 31 affected keys.

sources_opened.title: Plan National de Développement du Burundi 2018-2027
sources_opened.location: Section 3.1, extracted PDF page index 42 (printed page 43), paragraph 71; search result checked against the actual opened PDF text.
sources_opened.specific_text: The plan describes administrative redistricting as leading to creation of Rumonge Province and delimitation/regrouping of Bujumbura Mairie communes into Muha, Ntahangwa, and Mukaza.
sources_opened.implication_limit: Official government planning text corroborates that a regrouping occurred, but supplies no old-to-new neighborhood, locality, or polygon membership table and no dated geographic boundary source.

sources_opened.title: Loi n°1/33 du 28 novembre 2014 portant révision de la Loi n°1/02 du 25 janvier 2010 portant organisation de l’administration communale

sources_opened.implication_limit: The official listing establishes an enacted communal-administration revision and date, not the required exact boundary or predecessor-feature crosswalk.

queries_performed: Official-domain searches for Burundi decrees/laws dated 2014-2015 mentioning Bugarama, Muhuta, Muha, Ntahangwa, Rumonge, and administrative delimitation.
Exact-title searches for Loi n°1/10 du 26 mars 2015 and Loi n°1/33 du 28 novembre 2014.
Opened the official Presidency PND PDF and used text search for Muha, Ntahangwa, delimitation, and 2014.

Opened the official Presidency page for Loi n°1/33; its embedded 13,480,065-byte law PDF exceeded the web reader's size limit. A separate linked 31-page communal-law scan exposed only generic page headings, not relevant boundary clauses.
remaining_evidence_needed: For Bugarama (19 water keys) and Muhuta (12 land keys): the 2015 law confirms each named commune's limits were retained at the provincial transfer. The remaining source-specific question is whether the 2007-labeled retained feature geometry is in fact the same feature/boundary version referred to by that law and how the 2023 enacted reorganization treated the historical feature identities; the 2015 law itself contains no map or capture/revision metadata.

For Muha and Ntahangwa: the enacted 2014/2015 instrument or official administrative record/map listing the predecessor localities or boundaries assigned to each new commune, joined to the original retained feature identities/geometries. PND paragraph 71 names the regrouping but not its exact membership.
For all four: evidence tying the source's 2007 metadata label to actual feature capture/revision dates and boundary identity; names alone do not resolve source-vintage applicability.

original_contract_assessment.interpretation: No separate predicate was found requiring every stable Atlas location ID to remain a top-level commune in the 2023 administrative hierarchy. For the 31 Bugarama/Muhuta keys, retained records identify exact source features Bugarama 21766830B31049489476840 -> owner 9019 (19 inland-water cells) and Muhuta 21766830B14140898215143 -> owner 8990 (12 land cells); both source-owner and reverse-lineage vectors match. The three frozen block-32 witness masks report the same source and physical class as those stable recorded targets; all 31 were within the previously computed 529 diagnostic-supported keys and outside the 54 held-key set. The 2015 law is positive evidence that their commune boundaries were retained during the province transfer. It does not prove the represented-year-2007 feature geometry is the precise boundary version referred to in 2015; however, this capture-date uncertainty is not more specific for these 31 cells than for the 448 already prepared for native authority. No distinct transfer-as-redraw predicate remains for these 31. They may proceed to the ordinary stable-location/constructor checks as a bounded candidate subset; this is not an automatic qualification, acceptance, or authorization to alter frozen PR 2654.
original_contract_assessment.status: Research finding only. No constructor, owner observation, physical run, or native diagnostic was rerun; frozen PR 2654 and its 135 held keys remain unchanged.
